environment.description: Same ECS Fargate deployment with Tomcat 9.0.68. The ALB target group has a Lambda@Edge-equivalent response transformation via CloudFront distribution (origin set to ALB) with a CloudFront Function on viewer-response event that appends headers. The function ID cf-fn-a8e2c1 injects a response header with directive 'default-src self' and 'script-src nonce-{random}' per-request, effectively requiring nonce-based script authorization. Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a response headers policy (ID: 67f7725c-6f97-4210-82d7-5512b31e9d03) of type 'SecurityHeadersPolicy' with CSP override enabled and frame-ancestors set to 'none'. The SQS queue still accepts cross-account messages. Note: the Tomcat server itself does NOT set CSP headers - they are injected at the CDN edge layer only, meaning the servlet code's inline script tag will also be blocked unless it carries the per-request nonce (which it does not, since the nonce is generated at the edge and not communicated back to origin).

config.infrastructure: ECS Fargate behind ALB, fronted by CloudFront distribution d-XXXXXXXXXXXX
config.note: CSP nonce is generated at edge; origin has no knowledge of it
